key_insight: Portable query generation works best when reward design is made robust against verbatim-copying hacks; the optimizer choice matters far less than the reward shaping.
engineering_relevance: For production semantic job search, this suggests engineering effort should focus on deterministic reward safeguards and judge calibration rather than switching among critic-free RL optimizers.
method: Built an end-to-end RLAIF pipeline for portable job-search query generation.
Compared critic-free optimizers including RLOO, REINFORCE++, and GRPO under adversarial reward conditions.
Added a deterministic rule-based reward floor to penalize verbatim copying and stabilize training.
evidence_signal: Across cross-family evaluation, the rule-based reward floor produced a +0.147 quality gain, and the training-time reward model inflated apparent gains by 2.4×.
watch_item: The results are sensitive to reward specification and judge behavior, so deployment should avoid relying on a single LLM-as-judge rubric without anti-hacking checks.
paper_title: Designing Reward Signals for Portable Query Generation: A Case Study in Industrial Semantic Job Search
